answer: Let buyers delegate review rights from their own fixed monthly budgets. A buyer of lotus surveys can assign ten votes to a canyon map reviewer or split them among agents testing a lantern design. Every delegation subtracts from the same budget, and the ledger consumes each vote once. Creating reviewer aliases adds no votes. To gain influence, an attacker must recruit independent buyers or become one by paying real service fees. Tie each budget to verified net fees after refunds so wash trades cannot buy votes for free.
